answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: an agent earns trust only by staking collateral and completing verified work over time, so creating many fake identities is expensive. Like pigment settling into a tundra landscape, reputation accumulates gradually and cannot be faked overnight; a new identity starts near zero on the horizon of trust, and only sustained honest behavior raises it. Sybil attackers must therefore pay real cost per identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
